title: Canonical finite Tate coordinates between diagonal and affine purity
statement:
Use the finite purity setting [def-pur-conventions] and its specified twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let F be the finite-field datum, C its coefficient datum, E a finite extension inside C's algebraic closure, and n>=0. Let Q be this existing setting at level n+1, with coefficient ring A=O_E/(varpi^(n+1)) in its existing sheaf-universe lift. For every k-scheme T with structural map a_T, let nu_T^* be exact etale-to-pro-etale comparison. The finite Tate site-descent normalization [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent] determines the unique isomorphism u_T : (mu_(ell^(n+2))^et tensor A) -> (mu_(ell^(n+1))^et tensor A)
whose value on every pure tensor is a tensor z |-> a tensor z^ell. Both powers annihilate A; no ramification-divisibility condition is imposed. Define the shifted-line comparison by applying single in degree zero, shift [2], and nu_T^* to u_T^(-1). Its target is precisely shiftedLine Q T of [def-pur-affine-space-comparison], whose exponent is ell^(n+2), and its source is the shifted ordinary finite line at exponent ell^(n+1). The ordinary constant coefficient and the diagonal coefficient power at degree zero have their canonical derived tensor-unit comparison: exact pullback commutes with single, followed by the ordinary comparison unit isomorphism and the derived single-unit isomorphism. Every change from these literal constructions to the recorded endpoint aliases is the uniquely specified transport with a heterogeneously equal isomorphism. These are coordinate isomorphisms, independent of either purity orientation.
